name: The Bride turned
text: North of Isseva on the mere the weavers walked their bride out this spring, the way they do, facing the water. Three weeks after, she was facing the land. Every bundle of her. Four men couldn't turn her, and nobody did. Orrin Vasse says the hem was wet to the knee.
variants: If the fog's down, go to the Bride with five marks and a knot. Orrin Vasse won't tell the Council, but she'll tell you.

name: Lights that want no oil
text: Ferrit Oache on the North Channel sells jars that light without oil. Green. They turn to look at you. The lantern-wrights buy them and don't say. The reedfolk say what's in them is what goes out of a drowned man when his lantern does.
variants: The wild wisps visit Oache's rack at night, like family at a sickbed. He says it's nothing.

name: A notch nobody cut
text: At Oulea there's a black needle the Builders left with a line cut round its top, and the Tide-Watchers notch the spring tides up a gauge on it. Hesk Vaurel found a notch above hers last month that she never cut. Mud on the plank. No footprints.
variants: Ask Hesk Vaurel what the line on the needle is. She'll say the flood. She won't say when.

name: A name in every rope
text: Every rope in Isseva has a name in it, walked in at Hask's wheel on the island past the Causeway. Corra Hask will walk yours in if you ask. There's a rope on her rack nine years waiting for her brother.
variants: A boat tied with a Hask rope never drifts. That's what they say, and nobody's come back to say different.

name: Five times round
text: South of Nauvissa there's a maze of reed hedges the reedfolk walk when they've lost somebody. Five times round to a pool, you say it to the water, you walk out. Edda Moye keeps it. She's never walked it herself; she says she's saving it.
variants: Somebody tied a name-cord on the Unwinding's pole in the spring and never came out the gate.

name: Herons don't drown
text: Pell Oduin by the Nave reads the herons for the Council. This week they all went west at dawn, to the old water past the Saltgate, and only half came back. He says herons don't drown. He's said it a lot this week.
variants: Sit with Pell Oduin at dawn and pay him five marks and the herons will tell you where something new's come into the fen.

name: One boot
text: Nelle Saye's big sundew in the tub by her door, the one her grandmother brought from Mor'oul: there was a boot on its rim one morning. Guild make. Laces tied. Nobody's missing, the Guild says.
variants: Feed the Mother Sundew an eel liver and Nelle Saye will bottle the dew off her for nothing. Use the tweezers.

name: None up
text: The Guild's Great Dredge west of Isseva dug down to a Builders' street under the peat, and three weeks ago the whole crew went down at the change of shift and none came up. Their cook keeps the pot on for fourteen every night. At night the bucket-chain moves.
variants: Wenna Corley chalks NONE UP on the Dredge's tally-board every morning. The Guild has told her to wait.

name: The barrow's stem
text: Out on the flats past the Saltgate the Salt Isles buried a king in his ship, and her stem and stern stick out of the turf. Hesk Vaurel at Oulea measures the stem every morning. It's turning toward the sea, a finger a night, and somebody's tied a mooring-rope to it.
variants: The drowned walk up the flats at night and stand by the Keel-Barrow like a crew waiting to go aboard.
